# The Industrial Revolution

## Origins

The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the second half of the eighteenth century. Textile production was one of the first industries to be mechanised. The steam engine, improved by James Watt in the 1770s, allowed factories to be built away from rivers. Coal supplied the energy for steam engines and for iron making.

## Consequences

Large numbers of people moved from the countryside to growing industrial towns. Factory work was often long, dangerous and poorly paid, especially for women and children. Over time laws were introduced to limit working hours and to restrict child labour. Average living standards rose in the long run, although the gains arrived unevenly and slowly.
